back: A foundation model specialized for language, pre-trained on massive amounts of text and able to perform many language tasks like summarizing, translating, and answering questions.
A large model pre-trained on broad, general data that can be adapted (via prompting or fine-tuning) to many different downstream tasks rather than just one.
The basic unit of text an LLM processes — a word or word-piece. In English a token is roughly three-quarters of a word.
An internal weight the model learns during training. Large models have billions of parameters; more parameters mean more capacity but higher cost to run.
A numeric representation of data (words, images, etc.) that captures meaning, so items with similar meaning sit close together and can be compared by semantic similarity.
The neural network architecture behind modern LLMs, introduced in 2017. Its key feature is self-attention, which lets it track context across a passage.
The transformer mechanism that weighs how strongly each token relates to every other token in the input, allowing the model to keep track of context and meaning.
Using an already-trained model to generate an output for a new input. Every prompt-and-response interaction is an example of inference.
Further training a pre-trained model on a smaller, specialized dataset to adapt its behavior to a specific domain or task.
The maximum amount of text (in tokens) a model can consider at once, including both the prompt and the response. Content beyond it is effectively forgotten.
A model that can accept and/or produce multiple types of data — such as text, images, audio, video, and code — often in combination.
When a model produces fluent, confident output that is factually wrong or entirely fabricated, such as inventing a citation or statistic.
Supervised learning trains on labeled data (inputs with correct answers); unsupervised learning finds structure, like clusters, in unlabeled data on its own.
Generative AI creates new content (text, images, code); predictive/discriminative AI classifies or predicts based on existing data (e.g., fraud/not fraud).
An image-generation approach that starts from random noise and progressively removes it, step by step, until a coherent image matching the prompt emerges.
The input text or instruction a user gives an LLM to guide its response. Clear, specific prompts produce more useful and relevant outputs.
